_: Machine-absolute path detection -- ONE authority, read by Python and PowerShell.
AIF task 'consolidate the local-path detectors'. Before this file there were NINE
independent regexes across tools/, each written for one call site:
ecoschema_map.py  manualgen/command_reference_candidate.py  reports/regression_index.py
reports/stage_public.py  fullstack_docs/audit_manual_publication_readiness.py
fullstack_docs/build_gptbase_bundle.py (x2)  datadict/disposition/artifact_disposition.py
staging/rebuild-staging.ps1
They did not agree, and the disagreements were not stylistic:
* ecoschema_map's lacked the lookbehind and read 'https://x64base.com/' as drive 's:',
which REFUSED a correct generator run (2026-08-13) and, worse, had silently rewritten
a published URL to 'http<local path>' for weeks before anyone noticed.
* SEVEN of the nine match only [A-Za-z]: drive letters. The project runs agents under
WSL and in mounted Linux sandboxes -- CLAUDE.md says so -- and 23 tracked files carry
/mnt/d/code/ccode or /home/<user>/ paths that those seven cannot see. The staging
overlay guard added 2026-08-13 was among the blind ones.
Regex syntax is restricted to what Python 're' and .NET both accept: character classes,
alternation, and (?<!...) lookbehind. No named groups, no possessives, no \p classes.
These are REPORT-ONLY signals by design. Some absolute paths are legitimate (host setup
docs, quoted engine output, SFTP examples against example.com). The tool names them; a
person decides. A guard that blocks on correct input teaches people to bypass it.

windows_drive.purpose: Any drive-rooted Windows path. The lookbehind is load-bearing: it stops the 's' of 'https' being read as a drive.

posix_host.purpose: Host paths as a WSL or sandboxed agent sees them. Absent from seven of the nine predecessors.

dev_roots_only.purpose: Narrower: only paths under a known development or staging root. Use where a broad match would be noise, e.g. the publication overlay.
